Date: Mon, 04 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CRM sanitation & confidence tagging — Q3 close readiness

Team,

Finance asked for a rapid CRM sanitation pass for opportunities that are forecasted in the Q3 close window. We need clean data (amounts, product/SKU, next steps) and a quick "confidence" tag so FP&A can finalize the pack. This needs to be completed by EOD Tuesday (2028-09-05) for the numbers to roll into the weekly close.

Please do the following for each open opportunity you own that is in Stage 3+ (Proposal, Negotiation, Commit):
- Verify Amount: confirm total ARR (no per-seat rounding) and update currency where applicable. Add a short note for any figures that are estimates.
- Confirm Product/SKU: populate the Product field with the canonical SKU from the attached checklist (crm-cleanup-checklist.csv). For multi-SKU deals, list the primary SKU + a brief breakdown in the notes.
- Next Step: set a single clear next step (Call, PO Requested, Drafting SOW, Legal Review) and add an expected date.
- Probability vs Confidence: set Probability (Salesforce probability field) as usual but add a Confidence tag in the 3-level format below (we've pushed a custom picklist):
  - High = probability >= 80% and confirmed internal/legal readiness
  - Medium = probability 40-79% and customer signaled intent
  - Low = probability < 40% or unclear next step

Quick rules: no backfilling with old estimates. If you don’t have a confirmed amount, mark the opportunity with "Amount: TBD" and add a note explaining how you’ll validate (customer PO, finance confirmation, internal pricing alignment).

I attached a CSV with the SKU canonical list and a short checklist. If anyone has a large multi-line opportunity (> $250k ARR) that needs special handling, loop me and Monica and we’ll triage.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: crm-cleanup-checklist.csv

Sounds good — we’ll run this across my book. Two quick clarifications:
1) Multi-product deals: do you want the total under Amount and then a line-item breakdown in the notes (recommended), or should we split into child opportunities? A few of mine are currently structured as one opportunity with three SKUs.
2) Rounding rules: ACME expects us to quote to the nearest dollar, but some internal pricing is per-seat and we round to the nearest 10s for quoting — which should we record?

I have a $320k deal where the customer will sign pending a PO; they’ve only given a ballpark. I’ll mark Amount: TBD unless we get the PO before EOD.

—Ben

Thanks Ben — good questions. Short answers:
- Keep the opportunity at the parent level for forecast purposes. Record the total ARR in Amount (nearest dollar). In the Notes section paste a 1–2 line breakdown by SKU: e.g., "Primary SKU: R-INF-100 (80%), Add-on: R-SEC-20 (20%) — see line items." We’ll use the Product field to store the primary SKU.
- Rounding: record the canonical quoted amount (nearest dollar). If you normally quote in tens for the customer-facing quote, still enter the actual expected ARR in Amount and note the quoted rounding in the notes.

Also: I’ll host a 20-min office hours tomorrow (Tue 2028-09-05) at 10:00 AM PT to walk through any hairy multi-SKU entries and to triage large deals. Calendar invite to follow. Monica and I will do a quick pass on any > $250k opps after EOD Tuesday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Karthik
